title: Smartphone Enabled Detection of Cognitive Motor Dissociation in the ICU
official: Smartphone Enabled Detection of Cognitive Motor Dissociation in the ICU
summary: The purpose of this research study is to evaluate whether a smartphone-enabled EEG (electroencephalography) system can be used to detect Cognitive Motor Dissociation (CMD) in patients with acute neurological injuries who appear unable to follow commands at the bedside. CMD occurs when a person may be conscious and able to understand instructions but cannot physically respond. The study will also examine whether CMD detection is associated with short-term and long-term recovery outcomes.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Admitted for acute traumatic brain injury, intracerebral or subarachnoid hemorrhage, or cardiac arrest
2. Neurological examination per Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R) criteria consistent with coma, vegetative state, or minimally conscious state minus (not explained by sedation)
3. Enrollment by day 7 post injury.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. EEG demonstrating ongoing seizures or ictal interictal continuum
2. Planned withdrawal of life sustaining therapy.
